vocabulary.meaning_en: complete, 100%, seen as one unit (countable nouns)
the same as "whole", but more formal or stronger
the whole amount; used with countable and uncountable nouns
vocabulary.example: All of the water is gone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: each member of a group, seen as similar
vocabulary.example: Every meal comes with a toy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: every single one, seen as different and individual
vocabulary.example: Each toy has its own special number.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a noun you can count: apple, room, pizza
a noun you can't count: water, salt, money, time
a strong, sudden expression of feeling (!)
food put on top of a pizza or dessert
vocabulary.example: Each pizza had a different topping.

fine_lines.title: whole vs entire
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى نفسه (100%، الشيء كاملًا) ومع الأسماء المعدودة. entire أكثر رسمية وأقوى، وتُستعمل للتعجب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning (100%, the complete thing), with countable nouns. "Entire" is more formal and stronger, good for exclamations.

fine_lines.title: whole vs all
fine_lines.explanation_ar: whole للأسماء المعدودة فقط (the whole apple). all للمعدود وغير المعدود (all of the water, all of the money, all of the people). all أكثر شيوعًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Whole" is only for countable nouns (the whole apple). "All" works with countable and uncountable nouns (all of the water, all of the money, all of the people). "All" is more common.

examples.sentence: All of the salt is gone.

fine_lines.title: every vs each
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما لأجزاء مجموعة من أشياء معدودة. every تركز على التشابه (المجموعة ككل). each تركز على الاختلاف والتفرد (كل واحد مختلف).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both are for parts of a group of countable things. "Every" focuses on similarity (the group). "Each" focuses on differences (each one is unique).

examples.sentence: Everyone in the room believes education is important.
Each one of you has different dreams.

expressions.example: I can eat the whole thing in two minutes.
I go to that café all of the time.
Each one of you will get a certificate.

grammar.title: Complete things: whole, entire, all
grammar.explanation_ar: لنتكلم عن الشيء كاملًا كوحدة واحدة نستعمل whole أو entire (للمعدود فقط)، أو all (للمعدود وغير المعدود). all غالبًا مع of: all of the money.
grammar.explanation_en: To talk about something complete, as one unit: whole or entire (countable only), or all (countable and uncountable). "All" often takes "of": all of the money.
examples: the whole apple / the entire room
all of the water / all of the people

grammar.title: Parts of a group: every and each
grammar.explanation_ar: لنتكلم عن أجزاء المجموعة نستعمل every أو each مع الأسماء المعدودة فقط (لا نقول every water). every للأجزاء المتشابهة، و each للأجزاء المختلفة المميزة. يأتي بعدهما اسم مفرد.
grammar.explanation_en: To talk about the parts of a group, use every or each, only with countable nouns (not "every water"). "Every" for similar parts; "each" for different, special parts. Both take a singular noun.
examples: Every meal comes with a toy.
Each toy has its own special number.

grammar.title: Common mistakes
grammar.explanation_ar: ✗ every of the time → ✓ all of the time (الوقت غير معدود). ✗ the each thing → ✓ the whole thing. ✗ Whole meal comes... → ✓ Every meal comes... ✗ All one of them → ✓ Each one of them.
grammar.explanation_en: ✗ every of the time → ✓ all of the time (time is uncountable). ✗ the each thing → ✓ the whole thing. ✗ Whole meal comes... → ✓ Every meal comes... ✗ All one of them → ✓ Each one of them.
examples: I go there all of the time.
I can eat the whole thing.
Each one of them is different.

questions.question: "I go to that café ___ the time."
questions.explanation_ar: الوقت غير معدود: all of the time.
questions.explanation_en: Time is uncountable: all of the time.

questions.question: "I can eat the ___ thing in two minutes."
questions.explanation_en: The complete thing as one unit: whole.

questions.question: "___ meal comes with a toy." (all the meals are the same)
"The toys are all different. ___ one of them has its own number."
Which word is a more formal "whole"?
Which is wrong?
questions.explanation_ar: every لا تأتي مع غير المعدود.
questions.explanation_en: "Every" can't go with an uncountable noun.
